notes: Spec asserts: a synchronous slash command renders locally with no model call, so state stays ready and no →working transition fires for the slash itself. For copilot the mechanism is the CLEANEST of the three shapes seen so far: the TUI's slash dispatcher handles the input and returns {handled:true} without ever entering the prompt path that emits user.message (app.js ~7800573), and /usage's action is an add-timeline-entry that resolves to the React timeline's addEphemeralEntry (~8516764/~8634781) — in-memory UI state. Nothing is appended to events.jsonl, so the daemon sees no transcript activity at all; contrast claudecode (a <local-command> wrapper its parser must filter) and aider (the slash logged as a real user prompt, which does flicker working). Belt and braces: every event type other than user.message and assistant.turn_end is Skip in core/adapters/inbound/agents/copilot/parser.go, so even a stray lifecycle line in the window could not move state. The warm-up turn goes FIRST and is mandatory — copilot writes events.jsonl only once the first prompt lands, so without it there is no real session to assert against. PRESESSION SHAPE (provisional, from code, same as the copilot basic-turn cell): the process scanner mints proc-<PID> before events.jsonl exists, so the birth is two phases and every later phase anchors to the REAL session. After warm_turn_end returns to ready, slash_window pins ready with duration_at_least_ms:5000 and invariants forbidding state_transition to working/waiting — exactly what would fire if /usage (incorrectly) drove a turn. OBSERVATIONS: the warm-up turn supplies live tokens (assistant.message.outputTokens) and cost through the shared price map; model is NOT pinned because --model accepts only "auto" and session.auto_mode_resolved picks per turn.
